ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: There are three small figures in the picture; Figure 3 on the right marks the line y=-x-1, and point P is drawn to the lower right of point B; A is on the positive x-axis, B is on the positive y-axis, and segment BA is a slanted line from B down to the right to A. Then reason: From the intersections of the line y=-1/2 x+2 with the coordinate axes, it can be obtained that, let y=0, x=4, so A=(4,0); let x=0, y=2, so B=(0,2). Therefore the slope of line BA is (0-2)/(4-0)=-1/2. Let the slope of BP be m. Because ∠ABP=45°, the formula for the angle between two straight lines gives |(m-(-1/2))/(1+m(-1/2))|=1, that is, |(m+1/2)/(1-m/2)|=1, solving gives m=1/3 or m=-3. According to Figure 3, P is located to the lower right of B, so BP should be a line descending to the right, so take m=-3. Thus the equation of BP is y-2=-3(x-0), that is, y=-3x+2. Also P is on y=-x-1, combining -3x+2=-x-1 gives -2x=-3, x=3/2; substituting into y=-x-1 gives y=-5/2. Therefore P=(3/2,-5/2).
